End User License Agreement (EULA)

Effective date: 12 November 2026

This End User License Agreement ("EULA") is between you and the developer of DevlogMaker ("we", "us"). It covers the DevlogMaker desktop application, including its bundled engine, updates, and documentation (the "App").

By installing, copying or using the App, you agree to this EULA. If you don't agree, don't install or use the App.

1. License

The App is free. Subject to this EULA, we grant you a personal, worldwide, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable license to download, install and use the App on computers you own or control, for personal or commercial purposes, including making and publishing devlog videos about your own games or games you work on.

The AI features use services you choose and pay for yourself, under your own agreements with their providers: an ElevenLabs API key for narration, and either an Anthropic API key or Claude Desktop (with your own Claude plan) for the writing. Generated music is optional and uses your own Google Gemini API key.

Except as expressly allowed by this EULA, by the open-source licenses described in section 3, or by law that cannot be excluded, you may not:

  • sell, rent, lease, sublicense, or distribute the App, or offer it to others as a hosted or managed service (link to the official download page instead);

  • modify the App or create derivative works of it, or remove or change any copyright, trademark or license notices;
  • use the App to break the law or the usage policies of the services it connects to (for example Anthropic's Usage Policy and ElevenLabs' Prohibited Use Policy).

3. Open-source and third-party components

The App includes open-source software that is licensed to you under its own license terms, not this EULA. Those licenses take precedence over this EULA for those components, and nothing in this EULA limits your rights under them. Notable components include:

  • FFmpeg, which the App runs as a separate program. You can get the corresponding source code as described on the open-source licenses page, and you may replace or modify the bundled FFmpeg program.

  • Tauri and React (MIT and/or Apache 2.0 licenses), and other libraries.

The full list of components, their licenses and copyright notices is shipped with the App in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and summarised on the open-source licenses page.

4. Third-party services

The App connects to services provided by others, including Anthropic (Claude and Claude Desktop), ElevenLabs, Google (Gemini API and YouTube API Services), Discord, Bluesky and Mastodon. Those services are governed by their own terms, which you must follow, and you pay their providers directly where they charge. If you use the App's YouTube publishing feature, you agree to be bound by the YouTube Terms of Service; see the Google Privacy Policy, and revoke access at any time on the Google security settings page. We are not responsible for third-party services and don't control their availability or pricing.

5. Your content and data

You own your projects and the scripts, audio and videos you make with the App. The App works on files on your own computer, including your git repository; it reads your project and writes its own files inside .devlog/ and the folders it creates. Keep backups of your work. How data is handled is described in the Privacy Policy.

AI-generated scripts, text, voice and music can be inaccurate or resemble existing works. Review everything before you publish it. You are responsible for what you publish.

We may provide updates, and may stop providing them. This EULA applies to updates unless they come with different terms.

The App is licensed, not sold. We and our licensors keep all rights, title and interest in the App, including all intellectual property rights, except for the rights granted to you in this EULA and under the open-source licenses.

This EULA continues until terminated. You may end it at any time by uninstalling the App and deleting all copies. It ends automatically if you materially breach it. When it ends, you must stop using the App and delete it. Sections 3, 5, 7, 9 and 10 survive termination.
